data.name: Aim RPG
data.detailed_description:
AimRPG is a first-person aim trainer with an entire skilling RPG built around it. It could also be seen as an RPG which has actual fun and practical skilling methods, and not just clicking and waiting for a few minutes at a time.

Most aim trainers ask you to click dots for an hour and trust that it helped. Here, that hour builds something. The same precise clicking that lands a flick in your shooter also chops a yew tree; the same smooth tracking that holds a strafing enemy also cooks a perfect meal; the same target switching that saves a clutch also hammers three anvils at once. You leave a session with better aim and a level, a drop, and a place on the board.

Every action is a short, timed aim scenario, and every skill drills a different mechanic. Woodcutting and Mining are static clicking. Smithing is target switching. Cooking is pure tracking, where your time on target decides whether the meal passes, burns, or comes out perfect. Hunting throws bee swarms, scuttling crabs, orbiting ducks, bouncing slimes and closing thieves at you. Accuracy and combo scale your loot, so sloppy aim means a thinner haul.

The skills feed each other. Mine ore, smelt bars, smith knives and armour. Chop logs, craft planks, build the bow that finally one-shots a duck. Enemies have real HP, so gear changes how a scenario plays, not just what the numbers say — a thrown rock needs three hits where a bow needs one. Progression rewrites the aim challenge in front of you.

Then it bites back. Bosses hit hard enough to end a run and everything unbanked in it. The bosses feature unique and challenging mechanics, that will leave you coming back after every defeat, offering immense satisfaction on your first pass, as well as many farmable rare drops which significantly boost your progression in all skills.

And that rank is worth exactly as much as the board it sits on. This is where most aim trainers quietly give up — a benchmark score means nothing if anyone can fake it. Every run here is captured with high-resolution input telemetry, and the server re-simulates the replay to confirm nothing was altered. Layered on top: a client-side anti-cheat, hardware-level integrity checks, triggerbot and timing-manipulation detection, and input-device restrictions in ranked play. It's a depth of protection very few independent games have ever attempted, and we believe it makes this the most rigorously verified aim trainer you can play. Your rank isn't a number you claimed. It's a number that was proven.

Features

Aim training as the entire game loop — static clicking, dynamic clicking, tracking, target switching, movement reading and reaction scenarios, each attached to a skill worth levelling.

A deep skilling RPG — six skills at launch with more on the way, on an exponential curve that climbs well past 99. Full gathering-to-gear chains, 11 equipment slots, and mastery stats that permanently raise your yields. New inventive skills such as chemistry enhance other skills, significantly adding to the game's complexity. There are also alternative ways to level up certain tasks, such as 2D clicking in-menu scenarios for skills like crafting.

Loot that changes how you aim — weapons with real damage, attack speed and headshot multipliers, armour, food that keeps you alive, and rare drops gated behind boss kills.

Bosses, dungeons and an endless Stronghold — multi-phase fights with weak points and invulnerability windows, a hidden dungeon behind a rare key, and a survival mode that only opens on a flawless clear.

A real competitive ranking system — a separate, gear-free Benchmark Arena across four aim categories and nine rank tiers, with the whole threshold ladder visible, an overall rank that headlines your profile, and endless Practice that never submits. Popular benchmark ranks linked through your Steam account such as Viscose v2 or Voltaic are also displayed on your profile.

Quality of life changes - We're life-long gamers, and we actually played our own game a lot. There are many things that make your life easier, such as conveniently placed buttons, adjusting your sensitivity right next to the "play" button for each scenario, multiple levels of detail that are easy to switch between, custom hitsounds and crosshairs, hotkeys, and much more. It was all built for your convenience.

Anti-cheat built first, not bolted on — high-resolution input telemetry, server-side replay re-simulation, hardware integrity checks, triggerbot and timing-manipulation detection, and ranked input restrictions. Protection at a level almost no independent game attempts, because the leaderboards are the product.

Replays you can learn from — download and study any run on any board: routing, crosshair placement, pacing, and the exact FOV, sensitivity and gear behind it. Or spectate a player live to see their performance in real-time.

Built like a real aim trainer — sensitivity in cm/360 or converted straight from your shooter's own settings, adjustable FOV, custom crosshairs, distinct headshot and bodyshot hitsounds, combos that survive a single miss, and a stripped-back Tryhard mode with nothing on screen but the target.

AimRPG requires an internet connection: progression, loot and scoring are server-authoritative, which is what makes the leaderboards trustworthy. Nothing sold for real money will ever affect gameplay, progression or ranking.

data.short_description: An FPS aim trainer built inside a full skilling RPG. Click, track and flick to chop trees, mine ore, forge weapons and kill bosses. Level your skills, farm real loot, climb a ranked aim ladder and compete on replay-verified leaderboards. Your grind actually makes you better.

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: Windows 10 64-bit
  • Processor: Dual-core 2.0 GHz (Intel Core i3 / AMD equivalent)
  • Memory: 4 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Integrated graphics or better with OpenGL 3.3 / Vulkan support (older Intel iGPUs automatically use Compatibility mode)
  • Network: Broadband Internet connection
  • Storage: 1 GB available space
  • Additional Notes: Internet required, very old CPUs with no GPU might not be able to render in-game scenes.
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • OS: Windows 10 / 11 64-bit
  • Processor: Quad-core 3.0 GHz (Intel Core i5 / AMD Ryzen 5 or newer)
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: Vulkan-capable GPU (NVIDIA GTX 900 series / AMD RX 400 series / Intel Iris Xe or newer)
  • Network: Broadband Internet connection
  • Storage: 4 GB available space
  • Additional Notes: A high-refresh-rate monitor (144 Hz+) and a gaming mouse are recommended for the best aim-training experience.
